text:
marina: Heads-up — saw a strange perf regression from the autotuner when serving MQA models with our paged KV layout. tokens/sec down ~18% at seq=1024, but 0% reg at seq=2048. looks like the chosen kernel path is sequence-length-aware but blind to page/block alignment.
ryan: which HW + CUDA? can you paste the bench command and perf output?
marina: A100-80GB, CUDA 12.3, driver 535. bench command: `./infra/bench/serve_bench --model llama-mqa --kv-layout=paged --page-block=128 --seq=1024 --bs=1`
marina: sample output (truncated):
```
tokens/s: 42.1 (baseline 51.4)
90th latency: 78ms (baseline 62ms)
kernel chosen: gqa_mqa_paged_fastv2_block128
```
sam: interesting — flamegraph shows hot spot in `attn_block_reduce` and heavy shared-memory bank stalls. looks like when page blocks don't align to warp-friendly boundaries we hit bank-conflict fallback path.
anya: i wonder if the autotuner heuristics just pick the "fastv2" kernel for seqlen <= 1536 without inspecting physical KV stride / page occupancy. we should add a cheap stride-check to the tuner.
kevin: quick mitigation: try `--page-block=64` or set `REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=gqa_mqa_paged_safe`. I repro'd locally: switching to block=64 restores tokens/s to 50.8.
marina: confirmed on prod-like perf box — block=64 fixes it. but that increases memory fragmentation in some cases. need a more general fix.
ryan: can you attach perf counters? specifically L2_load_stalled, shared_mem_bank_conflicts, and gstalls.
sam: pasted counters to our perf dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/perf/1772223333 — shows bank_conflicts x4 when block=128 vs block=64.
perf-bot: automated benchmarks complete — 1772223333: seq=1024 block=128 tokens/s=42.1, seq=1024 block=64 tokens/s=50.8, seq=2048 block=128 tokens/s=49.9. full diff in the run artifacts. :robot_face: 
anya: proposed plan: (1) autotuner add a quick page-stride check -> prefer block sizes aligned to 32/64 warps, (2) add sequence-percentile-aware kernel scoring (not just single seqlen), (3) add a runtime metric in console for "kv_page_bank_conflict_rate" to catch regressions.
kevin: i'll open a small PR to change default pager hint to 64 and a followup to autotuner scoring. PR will include a micro-benchmark that asserts no >10% drop vs contiguous layout.
marina: also logging a short repro script under infra/bench and a note for oncall: if you see throughput drop for MQA at medium seqs try `REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE` before rolling back.
ryan: can we add an autotuner test that runs on two random page alignments during CI? even cheap would catch this.
kevin: agreed — i'll add two randomized seeds to the autotune unit and run the bank-conflict detector.
sam: aside: is this specific to Ampere or seen on other GPUs? i ran quick check on H100 and saw smaller impact (~6%), so it's architecture-dependent. add arch-aware weights in the tuner.
marina: good call. i'll file a ticket and assign to eng-runtime/auto-tuner. ticket: https://go.redwood/ticket/INF-1892.
anya: thanks team — once PR lands let's run a small canary in dedicated and watch the token/latency dashboards. :thumbsup:
kevin: PR opened: https://go.redwood/pr/4821 — patch changes default page-block to 64 and adds stride-check to tuner scoring.
marina: leaving notes for oncall and will follow up after canary. thanks all.
